chung.Description:
This course will explore existing modern typographical ideas and techniques and attempt to expand on students’ typographical range. Students will investigate the communication of content and the emotional qualities of text.
Students will further develop their visual and conceptual fluency and create integrated communication design solutions. Emphasis will be placed on using typography, aesthetics, and composition to construct meaningful imagery and effectively solve communication problems.
This course uses the art of typography, aesthetic element,..., to build up ideas and apply them in designing products for graphic design such as: publication, branding systems.

clo: Analyze and Apply Typographic Principles and Conventions: Understand and apply established typographic terminology, layout grids, alignment techniques and structural systems.
Employ Typography for Visual Hierarchy and Communication: Apply principles of hierarchy and dominance to create impactful typographic layouts that effectively convey meaning.
Develop Typographic Fluency and Best Practices: Demonstrate proficiency in typographic design, incorporating best practices for legibility and aesthetic impact.
Develop a Critical Eye for Typography: Analyze the historical and theoretical context of typography, and evaluate its role in design.
Evaluate and Refine Own Typographic Work: Critically assess own typographic designs and identify areas for improvement.

Practice 1 Designing a Book
Research + Individual Presentation

- Students can start with the simplest books: novels, memoirs, essays, and narrative nonfiction.Students are not allowed to choose a self-help book.
- Students research all the details inside and out of the book, then give the lecturer a short individual presentation.
- Time: 5-10 minutes per student

'INDIVIDUAL WORK
- Book construction: Each part of the book has its role to play and its assigned place in the whole.
- Cover design basics
- Fonts for text: There’s no bigger decision a designer makes than selecting the fonts that will be used for the book’s text.
- Fonts for display: Knowing how to choose and combine typefaces is critical for the designer.
- Architecture of the book page: Building pages and spreads is at the heart of book design.
- Non-text book elements: Every book incorporates elements that are outside the text itself, like notes, bibliographies, part- and chapter-opening pages, captions, sidebars, pull-quotes, and others. Each has to blend well with the rest of the book, and stand out when necessary.
- Minimum of 45 pages that included text.
